topic.readerProblem: A marketer or founder wants copy-paste ChatGPT prompts for SEO tasks that actually work, knows ChatGPT invents numbers, and also wants prompts that reveal whether ChatGPT recommends their brand.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether ChatGPT and other AI engines recommend a brand for unbranded buyer questions; the page's final group of prompts is a manual version of that check, grounded in AEOeye's audit records and in published research on answer variability.

assessment: The page gives 23 prompts in five groups (keyword work, briefs, on-page and technical, editing, brand checks), each with the specific check that catches its typical error, and a table matching output types to their source of truth. It separates prompts that test recall (brand-name questions) from prompts that test recommendation (unbranded buyer questions) and gives a repeat-run protocol. It rests on Google Search Central guidance on AI content and spam policies, an arXiv paper on why models hallucinate, the SparkToro consistency study, an arXiv measurement preprint, and AEOeye's own audit records (8 of 161 ChatGPT answers named the audited brand, small self-selected sample). It deliberately does not supply search volumes, claim that any prompt improves rankings, quote OpenAI help pages (they could not be fetched in this session), or claim FAQ rich results or schema effects on AI citations.

sources.supports: Defines generative engine optimization, also known as answer engine optimization, as the practice of improving visibility in responses generated by generative AI systems.
Defines prompt engineering as structuring natural-language inputs to produce specified outputs from a generative AI model.
Kalai, Nachum, Vempala and Zhang argue that language models hallucinate because training and evaluation procedures reward guessing over acknowledging uncertainty.

Generative AI output may contain inaccuracies (hallucinations); Google calls it critical to fact-check and review AI-generated content before publishing; generating many pages without adding value may violate the scaled content abuse policy.

Defines scaled content abuse as many pages generated for the primary purpose of manipulating search rankings and not helping users; lists using generative AI tools to generate many pages without adding value as an example.
Title links are truncated as needed to fit the device width and Google may automatically generate a different title link.
robots.txt tells crawlers which URLs they can access and is not a mechanism for keeping a page out of Google.
With a permanent redirect the indexing pipeline uses the redirect as a signal that the target should be canonical; temporary redirects do not.
Google asks whether content demonstrates first-hand expertise, for example from having used a product or service.
The Schema Markup Validator exists on schema.org as a tool for checking structured data (page does not describe itself further; used only as a named checking tool, no claim made).
600 volunteers ran 12 prompts a combined 2,961 times across three AI tools; below a 1 in 100 chance that ChatGPT or Google's AI returns the same brand list in any two responses.

Schulte, Bleeker and Kaufmann (April 2026): single measurements are unreliable; Swiss-market prompts across four engines; ChatGPT used web search for only some queries and 57.8% of its runs had zero citations; at 7 runs the 95% CI on a brand's detection rate is about ±0.158 and the authors advise at least 7 runs per prompt per day (checked in the paper's HTML full text).
The Search Console Performance report shows clicks, impressions, CTR and average position, and can be grouped by query.
